auxiliary_material: The study outlines specific eligibility criteria relevant to microbiome integrity, such as excluding patients with recent antibiotic use (within 21 days), active inflammatory bowel disease, or prior bariatric surgery that disrupts the gastrointestinal lumen. It describes the intervention logistics, including a 1-week equilibration period and meals prepared by a Bionutrition Core to ensure isocaloric and macronutrient-controlled conditions. The authors hypothesize a mechanism where dietary fiber increases short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), which may enhance T-cell memory potential via epigenetic regulation, providing a theoretical framework for the mediation analysis planned in future results.
outline_action: Cite this protocol to confirm the design and registration of the DIET trial (NCT04645680) and to document that microbiome mediation results are pending. Use the detailed methods section to describe the planned 'gold standard' controlled feeding approach in the review's methodology section. Monitor ClinicalTrials.gov or subsequent publications from the MD Anderson group for the release of primary outcome data and mediation analyses. Do not present the hypothesized mechanisms (e.g., SCFA-T cell axis) as proven findings from this trial.
remaining_gap: Specific gut microbiome compositional or functional changes associated with the dietary intervention are not reported, as the study has not yet generated or analyzed outcome data (success criteria 1 and 2 remain open). There is no statistical mediation analysis linking microbiome changes to ICI clinical outcomes (ORR, PFS, OS) available in this text. It remains unknown whether the planned analyses will demonstrate a statistically significant mediation effect upon completion.
useful_material: This study is a protocol publication for the DIET trial (NCT04645680), a randomized, double-blind, controlled feeding study comparing a high-fiber dietary intervention (50 g/day) to a control diet (20 g/day) in melanoma patients receiving immune checkpoint blockade. The authors explicitly state in the Data Availability section that 'No datasets were generated or analysed during the current study,' which serves as an explicit statement that microbiome mediation data is currently pending/unavailable in this report (addressing success criterion 3). The text details the planned methodology to address the gap, including whole-genome shotgun sequencing of stool samples, metabolomic profiling (SCFAs, bile acids), and planned statistical analyses to explore associations between microbiome profiles and clinical outcomes (ORR, PFS).
